CHIEF COMPLAINT
Acne on the face

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Kayla is a 18-year-old female presenting with acne on the face that started approximately two years ago and is present most every day. She reports acne is not too bad on the chest or back. She has been using Persa-gel and washing regularly, which she reports helps somewhat. She denies associated symptoms including itching, bleeding, or pain. Current skincare routine includes washing face with water and washcloth in the morning, using ELF Super Clarity cleanser if skin feels greasy. At night, she uses ELF Super Clarity cleanser, toner, and Persa-gel. She describes today as a good day for her acne. She denies flare of acne with her menstrual cycle. Mother notes the biggest acne flare occurred when patient started school sports in the fall with increased sweating. Mother also notes patient has been compliant with facial care regimen but it has not been as effective as desired.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies itching, bleeding, pain, or other associated symptoms. Menses regular for approximately two years.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
No significant past medical history documented.

MEDICATIONS
Persa-gel (over-the-counter benzoyl peroxide)
ELF Super Clarity cleanser

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
No additional family history noted.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives with parents and sister. Has dog, bird, and bunnies at home. In 7th grade. Plays basketball, volleyball, and tap dancing. Wears sunscreen SPF 30 in summer.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Full exam performed except under underwear and bra. Multiple benign nevi on trunk and extremities. Scattered skin-colored papules. Open and closed comedones noted. Erythematous papules on face, primarily on forehead with some on central cheeks and chin. Chest and back relatively spared. Remainder of exam normal.

RESULTS
Physical exam findings as documented above.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Mild to moderate acne, mostly comedonal with small inflammatory component. 

Recommended skincare regimen:
- Morning: Wash face with mild cleanser, then apply noncomedogenic moisturizer with SPF 30 or higher
- Evening: Wash face with mild cleanser, allow to dry, apply adapalene 0.1% cream in thin layer to affected areas starting a few nights per week and gradually increasing to nightly use. If cost prohibitive or not covered by insurance, may substitute with alternative over-the-counter retinoid gel. Follow with Clean and Clear Persa-gel in thin layer, then noncomedogenic moisturizer.

Patient counseled on need for sun protection when using adapalene and that medication may cause dryness or irritation. Multiple benign moles noted on exam; all appear normal with no worrisome features. Follow up in six months to assess progress. Patient to call office with any questions or concerns before next visit.
